items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1969-05-30
items.q: Anyway, by me teaching these fellas, Mike said, well I'm going to keep y'all. I want this band.

ctx.x: And you think back, they were calling you Professor Longhand when I used to follow him.

No, let me tell you when they started calling me Professor Longhand. We were down here at the Caledonia Inn playing Bixley, me, and Eight Man Black was on saxophone. And I just remember who all, well I had this little kid with me like I said, little Papu, Walter Nelson. It was we four. I had long hair then. Slick had, his hair was long but it wasn't quite as long as mine then. My hair was as long as you. All of that, then I was wearing that then. Them days was against the law. Anyway, by me teaching these fellas,…

Did you ever know any country blues players? Any pickers or anything like that? Any bottleneck players? Like I said, I met a lot of them. Chad Atkins. I don't know whether you call him a country man. I hear. He's good, man. He's a really good guitar player.

items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1978-Fall Transcript
items.q: So I got a job for a fella by the name of Mike Tinsitore. And he was very interested in my music, and he wanted to give me a job, and he accepted it, but he just didn't like the name Longhair. So he changed it to Professor.

ctx.x: Fess, something I guess a lot of people, especially those who aren't from New Orleans, would like to know, WTUL having a lot of student listeners who aren't from around here. How did you ever get the name, Professor Longhair?

Well, when I was dancing, of course, when it began, I was dancing. It was called Whirlwind when I was dancing. And I decided to quit dancing and go into the music field. So I left. From up in the direction where I was staying, went across Canal Street, way down around the Seventh-Oo-Six-Wars. People that didn't know me down there, at that time I was wearing long, long hair. And this is where they would approach me, say, Longhair, what is really your name? And I told them my name, but it didn't do any good,…

It's funny, the first time I think I saw you was at Tulane, so that's very appropriate. Yeah, we have a little bit of Professor and all. Where'd you grow up, what part of town did you grow up in? Were you, you weren't born in New Orleans, were you?
